explain.apply: Merge the run's branch into your current branch with a merge commit and remove its worktree. It refuses if you have uncommitted changes.
explain.discard: Delete the run's worktree and branch. Your files are not touched.
explain.generic: Run '{command}'. Add --help to see its options.
explain.not_interactive: Not running because the terminal is not interactive.
explain.plan: Classify the task and show the route and the reasons. Nothing is executed (with --model-classify one cheap classifier call is made).
explain.run: Classify the task, choose a route of agents, run them in an isolated worktree (or read-only in place), verify the result with your commands, escalate on failure and record everything in the ledger. Your branch is not changed until you run 'timonel apply'.
explain.start: Check git, Node.js and the coding agents, explain each missing piece, and install or log in only after you confirm each step.
git_init.done: Git repository created with a first commit.
git_init.explain: {path} is not a git repository. Git keeps the history of your files; Timonel needs it to make changes on a separate branch that you review before keeping. Creating one runs 'git init' and saves the current files as a first commit. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
git_init.files: {count} files will be in the first commit.
git_init.gitignore_written: Wrote .gitignore (review it later and add what your project needs).
git_init.no_commit: Nothing was saved and no repository was left behind. Add those files to .gitignore and try again.
git_init.no_gitignore: There is no .gitignore: without one, files such as .env (secrets), node_modules or .venv would be saved in the history.
git_init.question: Create a git repository here?
git_init.risky: These files look like secrets or dependencies and should probably not be committed:
git_init.too_broad: Timonel will not create a repository in {path}: it is your home folder or one above it, and it would save private files such as .ssh or .aws. Open the project's own folder and try again.
git_init.too_many: That is more than Timonel will commit on its own ({count} files). Check that this is the project folder, adjust .gitignore and commit yourself with git.

learn.agent.body: A coding agent is a command-line program (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI...) that reads your code and edits it from a prompt. Timonel does not edit code itself: it chooses which agent and model to call, runs it, checks the result and escalates if needed.
learn.agent.title: Agent
learn.budget.body: A budget limits spending per agent and per day, week or month, in dollars, tokens or requests. When one is reached Timonel skips that agent, asks you, or stops, as you configure.
learn.budget.title: Budget
learn.complexity.body: Every task gets a complexity from 1 (trivial, such as a typo) to 4 (architecture). Each level has its own ladder of agents and models: cheap ones for level 1, the strongest for level 4.
learn.complexity.title: Complexity tier
learn.escalation.body: When an attempt fails your checks (tests, lint, build), Timonel moves to a stronger tier and tells the next agent what failed. When an agent crashes, hangs or hits a usage limit, it tries the next agent of the same tier.
learn.escalation.title: Escalation
learn.ledger.body: A local SQLite file where every run, attempt, cost and outcome is stored. It powers statistics, savings and adaptive routing. It never leaves your computer; 'timonel purge' deletes old entries.
learn.ledger.title: Ledger
learn.privacy.body: Timonel sends no telemetry and makes no network calls of its own unless you configure a provider, a webhook or update checks. Secrets are redacted before anything is stored or shown.
learn.privacy.title: Privacy
learn.profile.body: A profile is a routing policy: 'cheap' starts lower and escalates less, 'balanced' is the default, 'max' starts at the top. You can create your own with 'timonel profiles create'.
learn.profile.title: Profile
learn.provider.body: A provider is an AI service reached over HTTP (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini API, OpenRouter, a local Ollama...). Providers cannot edit files, so Timonel only uses them to classify tasks, review diffs or plan subtasks.
learn.provider.title: Provider
learn.review.body: For harder tasks (tier 3 and up by default) a different agent reads the diff and approves or rejects it. A rejection gives the author one round to fix the issues.
learn.review.title: Cross review
learn.trust.body: A repository can include .timonel.yaml with commands to run. Timonel ignores it until you review it and run 'timonel trust', and ignores it again if the file changes.
learn.trust.title: Project trust
learn.worktree.body: A git worktree is a second working folder linked to the same repository, on its own branch. Timonel lets agents edit there (branch timonel/<id>), so your own folder is untouched until you run 'timonel apply'.
learn.worktree.title: Worktree
